intended_object: An index-bookkeeping helper. It sends a coordinate (r, p) on the diagonal p − r = k − 1 to the coordinate (r, p + 1) on the diagonal p − r = k, which is where the horizontal differential of the bicomplex starts. This is inferred from the docstring and from its use in `horizontal`.
explanation:
The definition is internal bookkeeping for building the differential of the product total complex. It is not a mathematical notion in its own right. It is used to state the horizontal component `horizontal`, which composes the differential d : X_{r,p+1} → X_{r,p} with the projection onto that coordinate. It is consistent with the conventions in this file:
- A pair (r, p) with p − r = k − 1 becomes (r, p + 1), and (p + 1) − r = k.
- The horizontal differential lowers p (`ComplexShape.down ℕ` in the inner index), so (r, p + 1) is the right source.

Since it is only an indexing helper, there is no textbook object to compare it with.
